subject: BridgeFlow x Redwood: trace connector pilot
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@bridgeflow.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: BridgeFlow x Redwood: tracing connector pilot?

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the intro at the partner summit. BridgeFlow builds a tracing + observability SDK focused on lightweight span propagation across LLM runtimes and downstream services. We've been running pilots with a couple ISVs that want cross-cloud trace continuity (edge SDK -> hosted runtime -> logging backend).

We think there is a clear fit with Redwood's smart routing + caching layer: a small BridgeFlow shim can instrument the Redwood runtime to emit structured spans tied to request_id and model_variant, and we can include out-of-the-box correlations for LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK calls your customers make.

High level ask: propose a 6-week joint pilot to deliver a Redwood Connector (server-side) + two sample SDK adapters (LangChain and a simple LlamaIndex connector) and an SLI dashboard. We'd like to scope a proof-of-value that shows:
- Per-request span linking from SDK -> Redwood runtime -> backend
- Minimal overhead (<2ms p50) for token streaming requests
- Example trace-driven alert that correlates latency regressions with model rollouts

Attached: bridgeflow-trace-spec.md (high-level API + proto sketch).

Can you put together the right folks on your side to discuss technical scope and timeline? We're flexible next week for a 30-45m sync.

Best,
Samir
Co-founder, BridgeFlow
attachments: bridgeflow-trace-spec.md

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@bridgeflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow x Redwood: tracing connector pilot?

Samir — thanks for the note and the spec. Appreciate the concise scope. I'm looping in Marissa (partner engineering) and Vanessa (product) so we can align on constraints and success metrics before a kickoff.

Couple quick clarifying items so we come prepared:
- For the "server-side connector" do you expect us to host a BridgeFlow process inside the Redwood runtime containers, or do you propose a plugin interface that Redwood implements and BridgeFlow ships the binary?
- SDK adapters: our customers primarily use LangChain (python/js) and some use LlamaIndex. Is your plan to ship adapters that sit in the client app and propagate headers, or to provide instrumented SDK packages we can reference?
- Security: any preferred auth patterns? We will need the connector to support short-lived mTLS certs or signed JWTs (we can provide an integration pattern).

We can do a 30m call on Wed 14th 11:00-11:30 PT or Thu 15th 14:00-14:45 PT. Which works for you?

I'll attach a quick draft SOW (redwood-pilot-sow-v0.1.pdf) with proposed milestones so we can iterate.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-pilot-sow-v0.1.pdf

From: Ethan Black <ethan@lchain.dev>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@bridgeflow.com>
Cc: Nadia Gomez <nadia@promptly.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow x Redwood: tracing connector pilot?

Thanks for including me — quick technical note from the LangChain side. Our typical instrumentation path is: user app (LLM chain call) -> LangChain's request layer -> outbound HTTP/gRPC call to model endpoint. For the adapter to be low-friction we'd prefer a tiny shim that:

1) injects a header trace-span: <trace-id>/<span-id> and an optional meta JSON in trace-meta header
2) exposes a fallback context manager for Python ("with bridgeflow.trace_context(...)") so existing code can opt in

Example (Python):
from bridgeflow import trace_context
with trace_context(request_id=rid):
    llm.predict(prompt)

We also want to make sure Keystone-style signed metadata is supported so the runtime can verify attributes (customer_id, model_pin).

Question: does Redwood surface a per-request request_id to the runtime API that we can use as the canonical correlation id? If so we can include that in the span and avoid sampling mismatch.

On the call we should bring a runtime engineer to confirm header passthrough during streaming and KV cache lookup spans.

— Ethan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BridgeFlow x Redwood: tracing connector pilot?

Forwarding our external thread — adding Jonas (solutions) to map telemetry surface points. Quick internal alignment and proposed action items before we speak to BridgeFlow: 

Action items (Marissa):
- Jonas to list runtime hooks we can safely expose (request_id, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, route_id, trace sampling flags) — due Mon 19th EOD
- Vanessa to mark success metrics in SOW (observable: end-to-end trace coverage %, p50 overhead, two demo scenarios) — due Mon 19th EOD
- Jordan to confirm partner commercial terms for pilot (credits, NDA addendum) — draft by Mon 19th

Notes:
- Runtime engineering caution: streaming token path is very latency-sensitive; avoid any blocking crypto ops in the hot path. We should favor async fire-and-forget emission or batched span flush.
- Security: BridgeFlow asked about signed JWTs — we prefer mTLS for server-to-server and short-lived signed JWTs for SDK-to-runtime header claims.

I'll consolidate before the kickoff.

-Marissa
Partner Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@bridgeflow.com>, Ethan Black <ethan@lchain.dev>, Nadia Gomez <nadia@promptly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BridgeFlow x Redwood: tracing connector pilot? — kickoff confirmed

Samir / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We're good to kick off the pilot next Thursday (28 Jan) 10:00-11:00 PT. Agenda: 1) Introductions & roles, 2) confirm scope & milestones from SOW, 3) runtime telemetry surface (Jonas), 4) SDK adapter plan (Ethan), 5) security/auth patterns (Vanessa), 6) next steps + repo/access.

Pre-reads (already shared in the drive): redwood-pilot-sow-v0.1.pdf, bridgeflow-trace-spec.md. I've also created the shared folder and the DocuSign envelope for the pilot agreement: https://app.docusign.com/doc/BRIDGEFLOW-REDWOOD-TS-2026. Please review and sign ahead if possible — we prefer to have the pilot agreement in place before dev work starts.

For the pilot success criteria we'll measure:
- End-to-end traces for 90% of synthetic test flows covering a LangChain chain + Redwood routing
- Observed p50 added latency < 2ms for token streaming (measured across 10k test requests)
- Dashboard that surfaces model_variant rollout correlated latency spikes (demoable)

Attachments: redeploy checklist, initial onboarding tasks (see Drive).

Looking forward — Jordan
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
attachments: redeploy-checklist.md
